reason: H0 does not fuzz optimizer-sequence text directly. It derives `optSequence` only from `_size` through `randomYulOptimiserSequence`, whose source alphabet is `DefaultYulOptimiserSteps`. Consequently, it cannot exercise arbitrary invalid characters handled by the new `removeInvalidCharacters` API or unknown abbreviations handled in `runSequence`, and it provides very limited coverage of bracket/colon normalization in `createValidSequence`.
evidence: H0 calls `randomYulOptimiserSequence(_size)` and passes its result to `OptimiserSettings::fuzz`; no input bytes are used as `yulOptimiserSteps`.
H0 rejects `_size > 600`, so optimizer configuration is selected from at most 601 deterministic size seeds rather than arbitrary fuzzer-controlled sequence strings.

`generateRandomPermutation` begins with `DefaultYulOptimiserSteps`, so generated characters already belong to the optimizer sequence alphabet and cannot contain arbitrary characters targeted by `removeInvalidCharacters`.
S1 adds `OptimiserSettings::removeInvalidCharacters(const std::string& _input)` with explicit filtering through `validCharacters`.

S1 changes `OptimiserSuite::runSequence` to catch `std::out_of_range` from `stepAbbreviationToNameMap().at(abbreviation)`, a path requiring an unknown abbreviation that H0's generated alphabet does not supply.
`createValidSequence` contains distinct unmatched-bracket and colon-handling logic, but H0 reaches it only through shuffled substrings of the fixed default sequence.
recommended_action: Add a harness entry path that derives an optimizer-sequence string from fuzz bytes, exercises `removeInvalidCharacters` and `createValidSequence`, and runs optimization with the resulting sequence; also explicitly cover unknown abbreviations and malformed bracket/colon combinations while checking for crashes, assertions, and stable handling.
